correctness.rationale: The 2026 source gives exact binomial-sum formulas for every proxy point mass and exact cardinalities for the proxy and true knot sets. Rewriting each summand as a fair-binomial point mass produces geometric weights tending to \((3/4)4^{-i}\). Uniform local De Moivre--Laplace on bounded standardized windows, together with a binomial maximal-mass bound and geometric-tail domination, yields the stated local Gaussian law for both parities. The odd-row center shift is constant and vanishes on the square-root scale. Exact source-set cardinalities make the palindromic transfer error \(O(2^{-c/2})\), negligible relative to \(c^{-1/2}\). Constants and lattice spacing were independently recomputed and regression-checked.

value.rationale: A local limit theorem is the natural next asymptotic layer beyond the source's CLT: it determines the actual frequency of individual signature values, which weak convergence cannot do. The result is uniform across every bounded central window and yields explicit asymptotic counts for all fixed even signatures, including signature zero. This provides a sharper benchmark for random-knot models and for questions conditioned on a specific signature, rather than a routine recomputation of a finite column.
